e-5479.worked_solution:
First, we find the matrix $\, A-\lambda I\mathbin{:}$
﻿﻿﻿![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14068962/assets/0c6f9f860a1cf4d510f6c3d4d9c66b77496a354bb1e2cef1b69fd1178e4f15ab.png)

e-5481.problem: Find all real eigenvalues of the matrix ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14068962/assets/a1b88b7897649bb059cef39d40b2b052a13ac28282223b5688a1bce98296fb53.png)
e-5481.worked_solution:
Let's start by writing the matrix $A - \lambda I\mathbin{:}$
﻿﻿![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14068962/assets/ca8f02e390e338b62956302ec45ea274ad73a51dafde3fe93b3d1e37dd663699.png)

Now, let's find and solve the characteristic equation $\det(A-\lambda I) = 0\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}10-\lambda  & 3 \\ 6 & 7-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (10-\lambda )(7-\lambda )-3\cdot 6 & =0 \\ 70-7\lambda -10\lambda +{\lambda }^{2}-18 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}-17\lambda +52 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Using the quadratic formula, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\lambda  & =\frac{17\pm \sqrt{(-17)^{2}-4\cdot 1\cdot 52}}{2\cdot 1} \\  & =\frac{17\pm \sqrt{81}}{2} \\  & =\frac{17\pm 9}{2} \\  & =13,4.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the eigenvalues are $\lambda=13$ and $\lambda=4.$

after.problem: Find the characteristic equation of the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 \\ -8 & -6\end{aligned}].$
after.worked_solution:
First, we find the matrix $\,A-\lambda I:$
﻿﻿﻿

$$
A-\lambda I=[\begin{aligned}2-\lambda  & 2 \\ -8 & -6-\lambda \end{aligned}].
$$

Then, the characteristic equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}2-\lambda  & 2 \\ -8 & -6-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (2-\lambda )(-6-\lambda )-(-8)\cdot 2 & =0 \\ -12-2\lambda +6\lambda +{\lambda }^{2}+16 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}+4\lambda +4 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

after.problem: Find the characteristic equation of the matrix $N=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 3 \\ 3 & -1\end{aligned}].$
after.worked_solution:
First, we find the matrix $\,N-\lambda I:$
﻿﻿﻿

$$
N-\lambda I=[\begin{aligned}-2-\lambda  & 3 \\ 3 & -1-\lambda \end{aligned}].
$$

Then, the characteristic equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}det(N-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}-2-\lambda  & 3 \\ 3 & -1-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (-2-\lambda )(-1-\lambda )-3\cdot 3 & =0 \\ 2+2\lambda +\lambda +{\lambda }^{2}-9 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}+3\lambda -7 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

after.problem:
Find the characteristic equation of the matrix 
$D=[\begin{aligned}5 & -5 \\ 4 & -7\end{aligned}].$
after.worked_solution:
First, we find the matrix $\,D-\lambda I:$
﻿﻿﻿

$$
D-\lambda I=[\begin{aligned}5-\lambda  & -5 \\ 4 & -7-\lambda \end{aligned}].
$$

Then, the characteristic equation is 

$$
\begin{aligned}det(D-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}5-\lambda  & -5 \\ 4 & -7-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (5-\lambda )(-7-\lambda )-(-5)\cdot 4 & =0 \\ -35-5\lambda +7\lambda +{\lambda }^{2}+20 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}+2\lambda -15 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 6
after.problem:
Find all real eigenvalues of the matrix
$M=[\begin{aligned}-4 & 5 \\ 5 & -4\end{aligned}].$
after.worked_solution:
Let's start by writing the matrix $M-\lambda I:$
﻿﻿﻿

$$
M-\lambda I=[\begin{aligned}-4-\lambda  & 5 \\ 5 & -4-\lambda \end{aligned}].
$$

Now, let's find and solve the characteristic equation $det(M-\lambda I)=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}det(M-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}-4-\lambda  & 5 \\ 5 & -4-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (-4-\lambda )(-4-\lambda )-5\cdot 5 & =0 \\ 16+4\lambda +4\lambda +{\lambda }^{2}-25 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}+8\lambda -9 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Using the quadratic formula, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\lambda  & =\frac{-8\pm \sqrt{{8}^{2}+4\cdot 1\cdot 9}}{2} \\  & =\frac{-8\pm \sqrt{100}}{2} \\  & =\frac{-8\pm 10}{2} \\  & =1,-9.\end{aligned}
$$

content.problem:
Find all real eigenvalues of the matrix
$M=[\begin{aligned}-4 & 5 \\ 5 & -4\end{aligned}].$
content.worked_solution:
Let's start by writing the matrix $M-\lambda I:$
﻿﻿﻿

$$
M-\lambda I=[\begin{aligned}-4-\lambda  & 5 \\ 5 & -4-\lambda \end{aligned}].
$$

Now, let's find and solve the characteristic equation $det(M-\lambda I)=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}det(M-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}-4-\lambda  & 5 \\ 5 & -4-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (-4-\lambda )(-4-\lambda )-5\cdot 5 & =0 \\ 16+4\lambda +4\lambda +{\lambda }^{2}-25 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}+8\lambda -9 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Using the quadratic formula, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\lambda  & =\frac{-8\pm \sqrt{{8}^{2}+4\cdot 1\cdot 9}}{2} \\  & =\frac{-8\pm \sqrt{100}}{2} \\  & =\frac{-8\pm 10}{2} \\  & =1,-9.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the eigenvalues are $\lambda =1$ and $\lambda =-9.$

after.problem:
Find all real eigenvalues of the matrix
$L=[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 \\ 5 & -1\end{aligned}].$
after.worked_solution:
Let's start by writing the matrix $L-\lambda I:$
﻿﻿﻿

$$
L-\lambda I=[\begin{aligned}2-\lambda  & 2 \\ 5 & -1-\lambda \end{aligned}].
$$

Now, let's find and solve the characteristic equation $det(L-\lambda I)=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}det(L-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}2-\lambda  & 2 \\ 5 & -1-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (2-\lambda )(-1-\lambda )-5\cdot 2 & =0 \\ -2+\lambda -2\lambda +{\lambda }^{2}-10 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}-\lambda -12 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Using the quadratic formula, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\lambda  & =\frac{1\pm \sqrt{(-1)^{2}+4\cdot 1\cdot 12}}{2} \\  & =\frac{1\pm \sqrt{49}}{2} \\  & =\frac{1\pm 7}{2} \\  & =-3,4.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the eigenvalues are $\lambda =-3$ and $\lambda =4.$

content.problem:
Find all real eigenvalues of the matrix
$D=[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 \\ 2 & 3\end{aligned}].$
content.worked_solution:
Let's start by writing the matrix $D-\lambda I:$
﻿﻿

$$
D-\lambda I=[\begin{aligned}3-\lambda  & 2 \\ 2 & 3-\lambda \end{aligned}].
$$

Now, let's find and solve the characteristic equation $det(D-\lambda I)=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}det(D-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}3-\lambda  & 2 \\ 2 & 3-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (3-\lambda )(3-\lambda )-2\cdot 2 & =0 \\ 9-3\lambda -3\lambda +{\lambda }^{2}-4 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}-6\lambda +5 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Using the quadratic formula, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\lambda  & =\frac{6\pm \sqrt{(-6)^{2}-4\cdot 1\cdot 5}}{2} \\  & =\frac{6\pm \sqrt{16}}{2} \\  & =\frac{6\pm 4}{2} \\  & =5,1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the eigenvalues are $\lambda =5$ and $\lambda =1.$
